options.text: Resistance of a wire depends on the length and density of the wire.
Specific resistance is the same for all conductors.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Resistance of a wire depends on the length and cross-section of the wire**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__Concept:__

Electric current is the flow of electric charges through a particular area of a conductor( a metallic wire) in unit time.

Electric current is mathematically expressed as:

__
 
• I=Q/t,

I= current, Q= net charge flowing across any cross-section of the conductor, and t= time

 
• For electric current to flow through a conductor, there should be a potential difference between two points in the conductor.
 
• The electric potential difference is the work done to move a unit charge from one point to another in an electric circuit. V=W/Q, where, V is the potential difference, W is work done, and Q is the amount of charge flowing through the conductor. The S.I. unit of electric potential difference is volt(V).
 
• According to Ohm's law, the electric potential difference across the ends of a wire in a given electric circuit is directly proportional to the current flowing through it.
 
• V=IR, as V is the potential difference, I is current, R is Resistance

Resistance:

It is the ability of a conductor to resist the flow of charges through it when part of an electric circuit. The S.I unit of resistance is the ohm(Ω ).

The resistance of a conductor depends upon the following factors.

 
• On the length of the conductor
 
• On the area of cross-section of the conductor
 
• Nature of the material or resistivity.

Resistivity is the property of a material by virtue of which it resists the flow of charges through it. The S.I unit of resistivity is Ω m.
Explanation__:

The resistance of a conductor is calculated by the following equation

R= ρ× l/a

__
 
• R= resistance,p= resistivity, l= length of material, a= area of cross-section.

From the above equation, it is understood that 

 
• the resistance of a wire is directly proportional to the length of the wire and inversely proportional to the area of the cross-section.
 
• resistance can never be negative as length and area are positive quantities.
 
• resistance of the wire will remain constant for a given wire as the length and area of cross-section and resistivity remain constant.

questions.question: If the resistance in a circuit is increased while the voltage remains constant, the current will __________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**decrease**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• According to Ohm's Law, the current (I) in a circuit is directly proportional to the voltage (V) and inversely proportional to the resistance (R).
 
• Ohm's Law is mathematically represented as I = V/R.
 
• If the resistance (R) in the circuit increases while the voltage (V) remains constant, the current (I) must decrease.
 
• This relationship highlights that current and resistance are inversely related for a given constant voltage.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ohm's Law:** A fundamental principle in electronics and electrical engineering stating that V = IR, where V is voltage, I is current, and R is resistance.
 
• **Resistance:** A measure of the opposition to the flow of electric current, measured in ohms (Ω).
 
• **Voltage:** The electric potential difference between two points, which drives current through a circuit, measured in volts (V).
 
• **Current:** The flow of electric charge through a conductor, measured in amperes (A).
 
• **Inversely Proportional Relationship:** A relationship where an increase in one quantity leads to a decrease in another, and vice versa.

questions.question: The commercial unit of electrical energy is
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kilowatt-hour**__.

__**Explanation:**__

__
 
• **Electrical energy** refers to the **form of energy that is associated with the movement of electric charges, typically electrons, through a conductor such as a wire. **
 
• It is a type of energy that **can be easily converted into other forms, such as mechanical, heat, or light energy, depending on how it is used.**
 
• The **commercial unit of electrical energy is the "kilowatt-hour" (kWh)**__.
 
• This is the **standard unit used to measure and quantify the amount of electrical energy consumed or produced.**
 
• It is a measure of the amount of energy consumed or produced by using one kilowatt (1 kW) of power over the course of one hour.
 
• **1 Kilowatt hour = 3.6 x 10⁶ joule.**
 
• This unit is commonly used on electricity bills to determine the amount of energy used by consumers. 

Thus, __**the commercial unit of electrical energy is Kilowatt-hour.**__

questions.question: What is the electric potential at a point P due to a charge of 2 × 10⁻⁷ C located 9 cm away?
questions.solution:
__CONCEPT__ :

__
 
• Electric Potential (V): This is the amount of work needed to move a unit of electric charge from a reference point to a specific point in an electric field without producing an acceleration.

V= (1)/(4piepsilon_o)(q)/(r)

Where q = charge, ϵo = permittivity of free space., r = the distance from the charge

The value of (1)/(4piepsilon_o) = 9 × 10⁹

**CALCULATION:**__

**Given:**

 q = 2 × 10-7 C

r = 9 cm = 9 × 10⁻² m = 0.09 m

The electric potential is calculated by, 

V= (1)/(4piepsilon_o)(q)/(r)

V= 9 times 10⁹ times (frac{2 times 10⁻⁷}{0.09})

**V = 2 × 104 v**

questions.question: What happens to the current in a short circuit?
questions.solution:
The correct answer __**increases heavily.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• When the **torn plastic lining of neutral wires touches each other**, then an **electric short circuit happens** due to this direct touching of the two wires.
 
• **The current flowing** through the **wires increases heavily **because the **resistance **of the circuit formed is **very small.**
 
• **A short circuit** occurs when the **current **in the **circuit rises rapidly **and the electrical connection draws an **excessive amount of current from the supply.**
 
• **By Ohm's Law, V=IR, Since V remains the same and R is reduced significantly, the current suddenly increases.**
 
• During this time,** the current has a very large magnitude**. It occurs when the*** neutral and live wires come into contact.***
 
• **The live wire carries current to the appliance at high voltage.**
 
• **The neutral wire** completes the circuit and carries current away from the appliance.
 
• **Resistance **is a measure of *how hard it is for the current to flow through the circuit.*
 
• When **live wire touches neutral wire due to defect, worn out, or damaged wiring, the resistance becomes zero, and a large current flows through it, there will be a short circuit.**
 
• If the insulation on the wires in the circuit is damaged or the appliance is defective, the live and neutral wires come into direct contact, causing current to rise in the circuit and a short circuit to arise.
 
• In that case, the protective device such as a circuit breaker or line fuse is supposed to operate or trip.
 
• **A short circuit means there is no voltage difference between the two points in the circuit.**
 
• **It is characterized by infinitely small resistance.**
 
• **Hence by Ohm's law large current flows through it.**
 
• **So, at the time of the short circuit, the current in the circuit increases heavily.**

questions.question: Electric field can be defined as:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**force per unit charge**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• An **electric field** is a **region surrounding a charged object where another charged object experiences a force**.
 
• It is a **vector** field, meaning it has **both magnitude and direction**.
 
• **The strength of the electric field** is determined by the **magnitude of the charge creating it **and the **distance from the charge**.
 
• Electric fields can be visualized using** field lines**, which show the direction and strength of the field at different points.
 
• The electric field is responsible for the **movement of charged particles**, such as **electrons**, in a circuit.
 
• The **SI unit** for electric field strength is **volts per meter (V/m)**.
 
• Electric fields play a crucial role in many **technological applications**, such as in **electronics and telecommunications**.
 
• They are also important in understanding the** behavior of charged particles **in **physics and engineering contexts**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Energy per unit charge**, also known as electric potential or voltage, is measured in volts (V) and represents the amount of energy required to move a unit charge between two points in an electric field.
 
• **The force per unit charge**, measured in newtons per coulomb (N/C), represents the force experienced by a unit charge in an electric field.
 
• **Energy per unit current**, also known as electric potential difference or voltage, is measured in volts (V) and represents the amount of energy required to move a unit current through a circuit.

questions.question: What is the main purpose of a lightning conductor?

options.text: To provide a path for lightning to pass safely to the ground.

questions.solution:

__
 
• A **lightning conductor** is a metal rod or conductor mounted on a building and connected to the ground by a wire.
 
• It is designed to protect buildings from the destructive effects of lightning strikes.
 
• The lightning conductor provides a direct path for the electrical discharge to safely travel from the structure to the ground.
 
• It does not attract or repel lightning; it simply directs the electrical energy safely into the earth.
 
• Installing a lightning conductor significantly reduces the risk of fire and structural damage from lightning.

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

• They are also known as **lightning rods**.
 
• Proper installation and grounding of the conductor are crucial for its effectiveness.

questions.question: The resistance of a conductor of length 'L' and cross-section area 'A' is directly proportional to ________
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**L/A**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The resistance of a conductor is directly proportional to its length (L).
 
• It is inversely proportional to the cross-sectional area (A) of the conductor.
 
• Mathematically, resistance (R) is expressed as R = ρ(L/A), where ρ is the resistivity of the material.
 
• As the length of the conductor increases, the resistance increases.
 
• As the cross-sectional area increases, the resistance decreases.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• It is denoted by the symbol ρ (rho) and is measured in ohm-meters (Ω·m).

• Conductivity is the reciprocal of resistivity and measures a material's ability to conduct electric current.

__CONCEPT__:

__
 
• Ohm's Law: It states that the current through a conductor between two points is directly proportional to the voltage across the two points. It is given by the formula I = (V)/(R), where I is the current in amperes, V is the voltage in volts, and R is the resistance in ohms (Ω).

CALCULATION__:

Given that:

Voltage (V) = 9V

Resistance (R) = 10 kΩ = 10000 Ω

Using Ohm's Law, the current (I) through the resistor can be calculated as follows:

I = (V)/(R) = (9V)/(10000Omega) = 0.0009 A

To convert amperes to milliamperes (mA), we use the fact that 1A = 1000 mA. Therefore,

0.0009 A = 0.9 mA

Hence, the current flowing through the resistor is **0.9 mA.**

questions.question: Electric devices like laundry iron, electric toaster, electric oven, electric kettle and electric heater are based on which effect of electric current?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Heating effect**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The heating effect of electric current is utilized in devices like laundry iron, electric toaster, electric oven, electric kettle, and electric heater.
 
• When an electric current flows through a conductor, it produces heat due to the resistance to the flow of electrons in the conductor.
 
• The heat produced is directly proportional to the square of the current, the resistance of the conductor, and the time for which the current flows (Joule's law of heating).
 
• This principle is employed in various household appliances to generate heat for different purposes such as cooking, heating water, and ironing clothes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Chemical effect of electric current**

 
 
• When an electric current passes through a conducting solution, it causes chemical reactions. This is known as the chemical effect of electric current.
 
• Examples include electroplating, electrolysis, and battery operation.
 
 
 
• **Magnetic effect of electric current**
 
 
• An electric current flowing through a wire creates a magnetic field around it. This is known as the magnetic effect of electric current.
 
• Applications include electric motors, generators, and transformers.
 
 
 
• **Physiological effect of electric current**
 
 
• The physiological effect refers to the impact of electric current on living tissues.
 
• Electric shocks, nerve stimulation, and muscle contractions are examples of physiological effects.

questions.question: A light bulb working on a 18 V battery draws a current of 3 A. What will be the resistance of the bulb?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**6 Ω**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

We can use **Ohm's law to calculate the resistance of the bulb:**

Ohm's law states that the** current (I) through a conductor between two points is directly proportional to the voltage (V) across the two points, and inversely proportional to the resistance (R) between them:**

I = V / R

R = V / I

Where:

R = resistance in ohms (Ω)

V = voltage in volts (V)

I = current in amperes (A)

Given that the** voltage (V) is 18 V and the current (I) is 3 A, we can substitute these values into the equation to find the resistance (R):**

R = V / I

⇒ 18 V / 3 A = 6 Ω

Therefore, the resistance of the bulb is 6 ohms (Ω).

questions.question: An electric iron requires a _______ fuse to prevent short circuiting.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 5__** A**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• An electric iron typically requires a fuse to prevent short-circuiting and ensure safety.
 
• A 5** A fuse** is suitable for most household appliances like electric irons, ensuring that the** current does not exceed dangerous levels**.
 
• The fuse acts as a safety device,** disconnecting the power** in case the current exceeds the safe limit.
 
• Using the correct fuse rating is crucial for the safe and efficient operation of the electric iron.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Fuse:**

 
 
• **​**The fuse is a protective device used to prevent electrical overload damage due to excessive current.
 
• It consists of a metal wire or strip that melts when too much current flows through it, thereby interrupting the circuit.
 
• A typical fuse is rated by the maximum current it can safely carry without melting.
 
• The correct fuse rating ensures that the device is protected from potential damage due to overcurrent.
 
 
 
• **Short Circuit**
 
 
• **​**A short circuit occurs when there is a low resistance connection between two conductors supplying electrical power to a circuit.
 
• A short circuit can result in excessive current flow, which can cause overheating, fires, or damage to electrical components.
 
• Fuses and circuit breakers are designed to protect circuits from the dangers of short circuits.
 
 
 
• **Electric Iron**
 
 
• **​**An electric iron is a household appliance used to press clothes to remove wrinkles and creases.
 
• A typical electric iron has a heating element that gets hot when electric current flows through it.
 
• The temperature of the iron is controlled by a thermostat, which turns the heating element on and off to maintain the desired temperature.
 
• Using the correct fuse ensures that the electric iron operates safely and efficiently.

questions.question: What should be the characteristics of a fuse ?

options.text: Thin wire, low resistivity, low melting point
Thick wire, low resistivity, high melting point
Thin wire, high resistivity, low melting point
Thick wire, high resistivity, low melting point

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**option 3.**__

__**Explanation:**__

**Characteristics of a Fuse:**

 

__
 
• **Thin Wire:**

 
 
• **Fuses are typically made from thin wires**__ or ribbons of a specific material.
 
• The **thin wire ensures that the fuse heats up quickly **and** melts when excessive current flows through it. **
 
 
 
• **High Resistivity:**
 __
 
• The **material used in the fuse wire has high resistivity**, meaning it **resists the flow of electric current.**
 
• This resistance causes the wire to heat up when current passes through it. 
 
 
 
• **Low Melting Point:**
 
 
• A fuse is **made from a material with a low melting point** to ensure that** it melts quickly and breaks the circuit when excessive current flows through it.****​**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

A fuse wire is a safety device used in electric circuits. Its job is to melt and break the circuit if too much current flows, to prevent damage to appliances or danger like fire.

 

Now, here’s the important part:

 

The material used to make a fuse wire (like aluminium or tin) has low resistivity. That means it lets electric current flow easily. In other words, it’s a good conductor.

 

So, how can a wire made of a good conductor still have high resistance?

 

The answer lies in the shape and size of the wire:

 

R = ​ ρ(L/A)

 

 
• A longer wire has more resistance.
 
• A thinner wire (small cross-sectional area) also has more resistance.

 

So, even though the material itself conducts electricity well, the wire is made long and thin to give it high resistance. This way, when too much current flows, the wire heats up quickly and melts, breaking the circuit.

 

The resistance is made high by virtue of the dimensions or shape of the wire such as high length and low cross sectional area. you might get confused by the property of low resistivity of the material and think thus, that the fuse wire must also have low resistance.

questions.question: The resistance of a 10 m long copper wire is R ohm. What will be the resistance of a 5 m long copper wire?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**0.5R ohm**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The resistance **(R)** of a wire is directly proportional to its **length (L)** and inversely proportional to its **cross-sectional area (A)**.
 
• The relation is given by the formula: **R = ρ × (L / A)**, where **ρ** is the resistivity of the material.
 
• If the length of the wire is halved (from **10 m** to **5 m**), keeping the material and cross-sectional area constant, the resistance will also be halved.
 
• Hence, the resistance of the 5 m long copper wire will be **0.5R**, which is half the resistance of the 10 m long wire.
 
• This is because the resistance is directly proportional to the length of the wire, and reducing the length proportionally reduces the resistance.
 
• **Copper**, being a good conductor, has a low resistivity, ensuring minimal resistance even for longer wires.
 
• This principle is widely used in designing electrical systems, ensuring optimal wire lengths for specific applications.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Resistance and Length Relation**__

 __
 
• The resistance of a wire increases with its **length** because the electrons traveling through the material encounter more atoms and thus more resistance.
 
• This is an important principle for understanding the behavior of conductors and designing circuits.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Copper Wires**__
 
 
• **Copper wires** are widely used in electrical wiring due to their **high conductivity** and **low resistivity.**
 
• They are used in **power transmission, building wiring, motor windings, and telecommunications systems.**
 
• Copper is also durable and resistant to corrosion, making it ideal for long-term electrical applications.
